newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos, forwards hold, bonds idle, ecu/drs bid.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos, forwards hold, bonds idle, ecu/drs bid.

text.p: Greek depos were holding, forex forwards were fluctuating in tight ranges but for an uptick in nine-and 12-month tenors, bonds were idling and ecu/drachma was firmer in 309.60/70 in early quiet trade, dealers said.
Greek markets will be closed on Labour Day, May 1.
"Depos are little changed and forex forwards are holding with the exception of nine- and 12-month tenors which are up 15 pips on lower dollar rates," said a money market trader at a private bank.

Bank of Greece offered to drain up to 200 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent today. A pact of 250 billion drachmas is expiring today so that a net amount of about 50 billion drachmas is entering the system.

"I am puzzled by the central bank's move since there is already plenty of liquidity in the system," said a trader. "The only explanation I can find is that the central bank wants to help the finance ministry's two-year zeros on Friday."
Greece will issue two-year zeros at a pretax rate of 9.9 percent on Friday.
Bond traders said there was scant activity in the secondary market with prices holding.
"The outlook for bonds is good on expected further deceleration of inflation and improvements in public finances as well as favourable external conditions," said a bond trader at a private bank.
The mark was quoted at 158.25/35 from Wednesday's 158.425 fix, the dollar at 274.09/19 drachmas from 274.400 and the ecu at 309.01/11 from 309.400 drachmas.
"The drachma is weaker against the ecu trading in the 309.60/70 band in early dealings," said a forex trader in a foreign bank.
